key_insight: PISO tracks the unknown part of a gradient with a running residual estimate, turning partial gradient access plus function probes into an efficient zeroth-order optimization method.
engineering_relevance: The method is useful when only some derivatives are available in practice, such as performative learning, reinforcement learning, and bilevel problems with black-box lower levels.
method: Combine the known gradient component with a residual estimate for the missing part.
Center zeroth-order probes around the tracked residual to reduce variance from random directions.
Use a randomized sketch/momentum-style update with explicit contraction and batching options.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence and function-evaluation complexity guarantees, and says experiments across five settings show improved or competitive performance against baselines with comparable oracle access.
watch_item: Performance depends on the residual’s variation and the quality of the tracking estimate, so unstable residual dynamics or noisy evaluations may reduce the benefit.
paper_title: Partially Informed Stochastic Optimization via Zeroth-Order Residual Tracking
